topic: Euler’s Formula: Bridging Circles and Exponentials
target_audience: High school students with basic knowledge of trigonometry and complex numbers.

sections.title: The Mystery of Rotational Growth
lecture_lines: Exponents usually represent linear growth.
Multiplying by 'i' rotates vectors by ninety degrees.
Repeated rotations create circular motion.
animations: Create a rotating point on a complex plane unit circle. (Color: #FF5733)
Show exponential growth as moving outwards from the origin. (Color: #33FF57)
Animate combined rotational and outward motion as a spiral. (Color: #3357FF)

sections.title: Visualizing Taylor Series (The Bridge)
lecture_lines: Taylor series approximate complex functions as polynomials.
Summing e to the x terms creates curves.
Plugging 'ix' into the series reveals patterns.
The series separates into real and imaginary parts.
These parts reveal sine and cosine relationships.
animations: Overlay Taylor polynomial approximation for f(x). (Color: #FFFF00)
Show series terms adding up to the curve. (Color: #00FFFF)

sections.title: Euler’s Formula: The Geometric Key
lecture_lines: Euler's formula links exponentials to trigonometry.
The formula is e to the ix equals cos x plus i sin x.
Think of 'x' as an angle on a circle.
The result maps points on the unit circle.
Algebra and geometry meet here beautifully.
animations: Place point 1 on the complex plane. (Color: #FF00FF)
Rotate the point by angle theta. (Color: #FF00FF)

sections.title: The Beautiful Identity: e^(πi) = -1
lecture_lines: Set x to pi in Euler's formula.
Cosine of pi equals negative one.
Sine of pi equals zero.
The identity becomes e to the pi i equals -1.
This connects five fundamental constants.
animations: Set theta to pi on the complex plane. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Rotate to the position -1 on real axis. (Color: #FF0000)
Highlight the final identity equation on screen. (Color: #FFD700)

sections.title: Real-World Application: Signal Processing
lecture_lines: This formula defines modern signal processing.
Complex exponentials represent oscillating waves perfectly.
Technology converts signals into digital data using this logic.
animations: Show a sine wave input signal. (Color: #00FFFF)
Represent signal as a rotating vector in complex plane. (Color: #FF00FF)
Display frequency spectrum output of signal. (Color: #00FF00)
